handoffs.definition: A try is one accepted handover command (a `command` event with action `handover` and accepted true), keyed by command_id; all later events with that command_id belong to it. A success is a try whose flow emitted `handed` (the arm reached the hand and offered the item) or `set_down` (sharp items such as the scalpel are set on a safe spot by design); the same two events ledger.stats counts. A miss is a `missed` event in the try (retries are the `retries` field on handed/missed). A stop is a `stopped` event in the try. Time is request_to_hand_s on the `handed` event. Lighting and skill_source come from the try's own events (skill_source 'none' when the flow ended before one was chosen). Rate range is the Wilson 95% interval.
handoffs.why: The 24 real-tagged handed rows have median 0.42 s and span 0.41-0.43 s, matching the fake arm's median 0.42 s, with no misses or retries across 24 cases. They are the test real_tries_are_recorded_fake_ones_are_not in controller/test_flows.py (RecordingArm motion_s=0.1, auto_pull_s=0.2, fake_arm=False), which wrote to Atlas whenever the tests ran with MONGODB_URI set; no real SO-101 hands over in 0.4 s.

recommendations: gripper is the hottest motor: peak 55 C against a 60 C guard and a 70 C firmware limit. Nothing in the data reached the guard (hot events: 0).
With torque on and no motion, gripper warms fastest: 1.13 C/min. Holding is not free; every motor warms with torque on.
Plan for at most 291 s of continuous hold per pass (half of the 582 s the gripper needs from idle to the 60 C guard); then torque off or park.
Park or torque off between passes: motors fall about 0.36 C/min (median), so 60 C to 50 C takes about 28 min.
gripper and wrist_flex idle warmest (49 and 48 C against 46 C for elbow_flex): their idle temperature is not a fault, only their rise is.
No guard trips were recorded, so the guard values are untested on this data; keep COOL_TRIP at 60.

reads.rule: Reads are split into scored and unscored. Scored = tied to a printed prop in truth.json: tray_tag always (a failed read counts as scored-incorrect); count_sheet when it is ok and its tray id and item ids equal a truth sheet's; pack_label when it is ok and at least one label's lot (or item+lot) is in truth. Other ok reads (test-scenario sheets, lots like L-4471) are unscored (not a printed prop); failed count_sheet and pack_label reads are counted as failed, not scored. A scored read is correct when tray_tag: tray id equals a truth tray_id; count_sheet: items (id, expected, initial, closing) equal a truth sheet's; pack_label: every label's (item, lot) matches a truth label. accuracy = correct / scored. Live events carry no filename, so this is content matching, not per-file scoring.
